body:
Trade speculation continues to swirl around the star running back as Indianapolis shifts toward a rebuild ahead of the NFL trade deadline

        The trade deadline fire sale is on for the Indianapolis Colts, who made two of the NFL's biggest in-season moves of the year this week when they shipped Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers. With those two stars off the roster, the attention is squarely on running back Jonathan Taylor and whether he will be the next standout Colt to leave town.If Taylor has any say in the matter, he might remain in Indianapolis. He played each of his first six and a half professional seasons with the Colts and on Thursday said that he wants to stay with the team that drafted him in the second round in 2020.Taylor said that despite the losses of two critical players and the clear downward trajectory of a franchise that seems committed to a rebuild, he has not requested a trade."I haven't heard anything," Taylor said. "I can't control that. Obviously, like you guys know, I'm always proud to wear the horseshoe, proud to be here. Similar to Quenton and Buck. They were proud to wear the horseshoe. They were proud to be here. But obviously, circumstances may cause otherwise. Hopefully that day may not come, but I can't control that."
The potential of a trade is clearly weighing heavily on the Taylor household. Taylor's wife, Ayanna, spoke out about the trade buzz in a social media post, saying her "mind is spiraling."Taylor himself has to balance the uncertainty surrounding the trade deadline with his duties as the Colts' biggest star. He and the rest of his squad are gearing up for Sunday's divisional battle with the Jacksonville Jaguars. They enter Week 8 as sizable underdogs in the wake of the two blockbuster trades and are in danger of slipping further into the NFL's basement with additional losses tacked onto their already poor 2-5 record.As it becomes increasingly clear that the Colts are slipping out of contention for the playoffs, and with the franchise firing general manager Chris Ballard in the middle of the season, the biggest question is which additional players, if any, are on the trade block.
"Obviously, it was all speculation until stuff started happening," Taylor said. "Quenton, Buck, those guys are the gold standard of the NFL. Obviously the business side of things, that's where it sucks at. I wish some way, somehow, I could have done more. I wanted to win for those guys. We wanted to get it done here with those guys. Especially Q. He's part of the guys who laid the groundwork. They're definitely gonna be missed."Among the plethora of candidates to be dealt at the NFL trade deadline, Taylor might be the most impactful. He has twice led the league in rushing touchdowns (including as recently as last season) and paced the NFL in rushing yards in 2021 when he earned a first-team All-Pro selection. He is on pace this season to threaten his career high of 18 touchdowns, given that he already has eight on his ledger through seven games.The Colts will undoubtedly receive a high volume of calls about their star running back, if they have not already. The Minnesota Vikings may be the best fit of any potential suitor given their offensive needs and the urgency to capitalize on an elite defense, but numerous other teams could also be in the market for a running back upgrade before the Nov. 10 deadline.

body:
Hardy has recovered from a gunshot wound he suffered in the offseason and will see action on Saturday against Arkansas

        The Missouri backfield is getting major reinforcements for the home stretch, as star running back Ahmad Hardy will make his season debut on Saturday against Arkansas, sources confirmed to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. Back in May, Hardy suffered a gunshot wound while attending a concert in Mississippi. The rehab and recovery sidelined Hardy for Missouri's first seven games of the season, but he's been cleared to get back on the field this weekend.Earlier this week, coach Eli Drinkwitz announced on social media that Hardy returned to practice but didn't commit to his game status. On Wednesday night, Hardy wasn't listed on the Tigers' SEC availability report, which was an indication that he would be good to go against the Razorbacks.That's a huge boost for the Missouri offense coming out of the open date because Hardy was one of the best running backs in the country last season. In 2025, Hardy ranked second in the country and first among Power Four running backs with 1,649 rushing yards and 16 rushing touchdowns.
While Hardy has worked his way back, Jamal Roberts took over as the No. 1 option in the Missouri backfield, and he's thrived in that role. Roberts is eighth nationally with 867 rushing yards, and he's tied for 11th with eight rushing touchdowns.Two-headed monster in ColumbiaWith all due respect to Arkansas, Missouri probably doesn't need Hardy at full speed to beat the Razorbacks, but what if the team could get him ramped up for the home stretch in November?After this weekend, Missouri faces a three-game stretch that includes Texas, Georgia and Kentucky. Two of those defenses are elite, and the Wildcats are no pushover. The Tigers will need their offensie firing on all cylinders if they want to go on a late-season run.
Roberts has already been great for Missouri this season, but the rushing attack as a whole has been rather pedestrian. The Tigers are averaging just 161.3 rushing yards per game, which ranks ninth in the conference. Throw a healthy Hardy into the rotation, and that number should improve because no team will have a better one-two punch in the backfield.With Hardy working as the lead back in 2025, Missouri ranked 22nd in EPA per rush and sixth in yards per rush. This fall, the Tigers rank 121st and 74h in those categories, respectively.The addition of Hardy should allow Missouri to keepp Roberts fresh -- and vice versa. That explosive duo might allow the Tigers to wear down opponents over the course of four quarters. Pair a rejuvenated rushing attack with a passing game that has thrived with Austin Simmons at quarterback, and the Tigers become a very dangerous team.

title: WNBA Finals: Dream, backed by Atlanta crowd, rediscover their swagger, force Game 7 - CBS Sports
description: The circumstances of a Thursday afternoon game weren't ideal, but the Dream -- and the Atlanta crowd -- rose to t
body:
The circumstances of a Thursday afternoon game weren't ideal, but the Dream -- and the Atlanta crowd -- rose to the occasion
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 29, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:27 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        ATLANTA -- Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, less than 24 hours before a do-or-die WNBA Finals Game 6 for the Atlanta Dream, veteran forward DeWanna Bonner insisted that despite the Dream's recent shooting woes, the team would be "crazy to lose confidence" offensively at this point in the WNBA Finals."We've been taking those shots all series, so it's just a matter of knocking a couple down," Bonner said. "You start feeling good about yourself. The crowd started getting behind it. And then it's like, 'Here we go. Here go ATL basketball."As it turns out, in addition to being the third-leading scorer in WNBA history and the second-leading scorer in WNBA playoff history, the 39-year-old Bonner is also a prophet.The Dream beat the Golden State Valkyries 80-69 on Thursday afternoon to force the first Game 7 in WNBA history. There was a lot of outside noise from fans and critics alike heading into Game 6, which was played at 12:30 p.m. ET on Thursday because of an embarrassing web of scheduling conflicts, leadership failures and bureaucratic blame games that left everyone weighing bad options and trying to save face until the time was locked in and tickets went on sale Monday afternoon. 
But none of that noise held a candle to the noise made by a sold-out crowd in State Farm Arena at lunchtime."First, shout out to the crowd being able to come here at 12:30 on a Thursday," said Angel Reese, who had 15 points, 14 rebounds and six assists. "So many things going on in the world, from school to work to everything else. And we're just super thankful. We fed off their energy. They were loud from the beginning. So we're definitely thankful for that. But we wanted to make sure we maximize this opportunity."While the atmosphere in State Farm was phenomenal for Games 3 and 4 last week, this crowd brought an extra layer of enthusiasm from the start. Perhaps it was the desperation of an elimination game or the novelty of playing hooky from the monotony of midweek work and familial responsibilities to witness the Dream regain their swagger. Or maybe it was a concerted effort to drown out the doubts of anyone who had ever marginalized or counted out the Dream or the city of Atlanta or the WNBA or women's sports -- or even women as a collective -- for one magical afternoon. 
Whatever the reason for the extra energy and decibels, it created a tangible electricity -- it was deafeningly loud -- that seemed to jolt the Dream players to life.The Valkyries, who started and ended the game 40 minutes away from capturing the WNBA title in just the franchise's second year of existence, took a 2-0 lead on the second possession of the game on a Veronica Burton step back. But then Allisha Gray, who is playing this series with just eight healthy fingers after suffering a hand injury in Game 1 of the semifinals and has struggled with her shot, caught a pass from Reese 23 feet from the basket on the sidelines, evaded her defender, shot the ball and saw it hit the front of the rim, bounce high in the air, and roll into the hoop to give the Dream a 3-2 lead with 9:04 left in the first quarter. It was a sign of things to come: Golden State wouldn't sniff a lead for the rest of the game.
"It felt nice," Gray, who finished with a team-high 23 points, said when asked about how it felt to see that shot drop in. "My plan was to come out and be aggressive from the jump. My teammates were really on me to just play my game and having my back. So, I guess I got the shooter's roll. But the biggest thing was me staying locked in and stepping up to the challenge."Like Bonner said, once the Dream players saw a ball bounce their way, it snowballed. Rhyne Howard followed up Gray's 3-pointer with an emphatic block on Gabby Williams, then Naz Hillmon hit a 3-pointer that brought the roof down. The exclamation points just kept coming throughout the first quarter, with the Dream leading by as many as 25 before halftime. In the first quarter alone, the Dream shot 73.3% from the field and 75% from outside after barely cracking the 35% mark all series long. "All we needed was a little bit of swagger going into this, a little bit of confidence," Reese said.
T-Pain really drove the Dream's motto for the game home during his halftime performance -- probably the only 1:30 p.m. ET weekday performance of his career -- as he sang his iconic line, "All we do is win, win, win, no matter what." The Valkyries, to their credit, outscored the Dream in the second half and cut it to nine with just over a minute remaining. But just as tension started to seep into the celebration, it was broken by -- what else? -- a Gray 3-pointer that sealed the game. This one didn't need a shooter's roll; it was all net. As the buzzer sounded at 2:50 p.m. -- just about time for the midafternoon coffee break -- "ATL HOE" chants rang out so loudly at State Farm Arena that they will still be lingering in the air when the Atlanta Hawks take the same court for their game on Thursday night -- and likely long after that.
Game 7 will take place on Saturday at the Chase Center in San Francisco -- or, to put it more aptly, on Halloween at Ballhalla. The Dream still have a mighty tall mountain to climb if they want to capture the first WNBA title in franchise history. But on Thursday, all that mattered was that the Dream's year -- and the WNBA's 30th season -- didn't end with a matinee showing. This series finale will take place in primetime."Job's not done," Reese said. "We definitely can be happy about it for now, but we have more work to do. I think we definitely have another level that we can get to."

How to watch as these two teams take center stage on "Thursday Night Football" after Week 7 losses

        In the Week 8 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Green Bay Packers play host to the Carolina Panthers. The Packers enter this game off a disappointing loss to the division rival Detroit Lions, in a game they had multiple chances to win. Green Bay had won three in a row to salvage its season after a blowout loss to the Atlanta Falcons the last time the Packers played on Thursday night (Week 3), but they hit a bump in the road last week. Now, they're looking to make it four wins in five games.The Panthers are coming off an embarrassing blowout loss at the hands of the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Carolina was blasted 43-13 last week and was never truly competitive, falling down 17-0 early. However, the Panthers still sit at .500 after climbing that hump with their win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6. Now, they try to get back to their winning ways.Which of these two teams will get back in the win column? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.Where to watch Packers vs. Panthers liveDate: Thursday, Oct. 29 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ETLocation: Lambeau Field (Green Bay)Streaming: Amazon PrimeFollow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Packers -3/5, O/U 47.5 via DraftKings SportsbookWhen the Panthers have the ballThe Panthers limped to their worst offensive performance of the season last week, managing just 266 yards, 15 first downs and 13 points while turning the ball over four times. They had previously gained at least 340 yards in every game, gained at least 24 first downs in four of five, and scored 25-plus points in four of five. 
Bryce Young returned to poor form on Sunday, going only 14-of-27 for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, while also fumbling once. He's now completed south of 52% of his passes in back-to-back games and south of 55% in three of his last four, with the only exception being a game against the decrepit Lions pass defense. Young got off to a hot start to the season, but he's cooled off a bit as of late.The Packers have been a tough matchup for opposing quarterbacks this year. They're eighth in net passing yards per attempt, and they've yet to allow more than 296 net passing yards in any game this season. They've also allowed just nine touchdown passes against nine interceptions. Jonathan Gannon has been good at limiting what opponents can do through the air, for the most part. It is, however, worth noting that the Packers faced Carson Wentz, Geno Smith, Michael Penix Jr., Jalon Daniels and Tyson Bagent before getting Dak Prescott and Jared Goff over the last two weeks. So they haven't exactly done this against a murderer's row of opponents.Green Bay has gotten pressure at a below-average rate — no surprise with Micah Parsons still sidelined. Instead, the Packers have gotten by against the pass with sticky coverage and timely plays on the ball. Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse have been solid on the outside. Javon Bullard has played well in the slot, and the safeties are providing quality help over the top and in the middle of the field.
Carolina's passing game is mostly built outside the numbers with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker, though Young has thrown over the middle more this season than in past years. It'll be up to the skyscrapers on the perimeter to win their one-on-one matchups here in order to give Young room to throw, though he should have more time than he did last week thanks to Green Bay's relatively weaker pass rush. In the run game, the Panthers lean on Chuba Hubbard, who is averaging 4.8 yards per carry in a workhorse role in the absence of Jonathon Brooks. Hubbard only got seven carries in the negative game script last week, but you can likely expect the Panthers to try to "Establish The Run" here as a way to get their offense back on track. Green Bay has allowed only 3.9 yards per carry this season, though, so it might be tough, especially with right tackle Taylor Moton now on the sidelines.When the Packers have the ballThe Packers welcomed Josh Jacobs back to the lineup last week but still found themselves entirely unable to run the ball against the Lions. They totaled just 60 yards on the ground, with Jacobs himself carrying 11 times for only 36 yards. Green Bay is now averaging a pathetic 2.9 yards per carry on the season, which unsurprisingly ranks dead last in the league.
The Panthers, meanwhile, were run over by the Bucs last week. Bucky Irving and Co. blew past Carolina for a remarkable 258 yards on the ground, which was made all the more incredible by the fact that the Panthers had yielded just 81 rushing yards in their previous two games combined. Still, Carolina has allowed 5.2 yards per carry on the season now, which, to no surprise, ranks dead last. Almost 60% of the rushing yards the Panthers have allowed, though, came in their games against the Bucs and the Chicago Bears in Week 1. They've been fine-ish against the run otherwise.So, can the Packers run the ball with any degree of success here? If the recent history of this season is any indication, then the answer is probably not. Jacobs has been at or below 4.0 yards per carry in two of his last three full seasons, and spending six weeks on the commissioner's exempt list in the wake of a disturbing domestic violence incident probably didn't make him a more efficient runner. And the offensive line is still not a good run-blocking unit. So, the fate of the Packers' offense likely once again falls on the right shoulder of Jordan Love. 
Love has only completed 59.8% of his passes at an average of 7.4 yards per attempt this season, but he's been victimized by a league-high 21 drops, according to Tru Media. Love is attacking deep downfield consistently, with a 9.1-yard average depth of throw that ranks fourth-highest in the NFL. As such, he's created explosive plays (16-plus-yard gains) at the third-highest rate in the league among 33 qualified quarterbacks.He should see favorable matchups when he looks downfield on Thursday night. Panthers starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson remain out on injured reserve, which has left rookie Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans as the starting corners. But Evans is also out on Thursday night, meaning, well, I honestly don't even know who is going to step up in his absence. The Panthers elevated Marco Wilson from the practice squad, and they may need to shift Chau Smith-Wade outside. Either way, it's not a great situation for Carolina.Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, who is trending to play, should be able to find space down the field against these corners, and then it's just a matter of actually hanging onto the ball when Love puts it on them. Green Bay could have a big night through the air if the Packers can protect Love, which will be made easier by the absence of Panthers edge rusher Jaelan Phillips, who is also out for this game.
PredictionIt was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Watson and Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better as of late after a rough start to the season. Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17

title: Chiefs sticking with Harrison Butker despite struggles after signing Justin Tucker - CBS Sports
description: Tucker's perfect tryout turned heads, but Kansas City views the veteran as both insurance and a resource
body:
Tucker's perfect tryout turned heads, but Kansas City views the veteran as both insurance and a resource
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 29, 2026

    6:45 pm ET

        Despite the field goal issues that marred the first six games of the season and evolved into a disaster in Week 7, the Kansas City Chiefs do not intend to make a kicker change for Sunday's road game against the Denver Broncos. Coach Andy Reid said this week that Harrison Butker will "probably" retain his role as the team's kicker in Week 8, and special teams coordinator Dave Toub went a step further when he staunchly affirmed that Butker is the man for the job.Butker missed two field goal attempts in last week's 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks and is just 11-for-16 on the year. His 68.8% conversion rate is by far the worst of his otherwise stellar career.Those costly missed kicks prompted the Chiefs to seek outside help, and after they brought three candidates into their facility during the week, they signed free agent Justin Tucker to their practice squad. The eight-time All-Pro will not handle the kicking duties against the Broncos, though."Butker is our kicker," Toub said. "We're trying to improve Butker. We're trying to get Butker right. That's what this whole thing is about."
Toub said that Butker went 10-for-10 on his field goal attempts at Wednesday's practice despite 28-mph wind gusts in Kansas City.The idea behind adding Tucker to the practice squad goes further than simply having a backup option should Butker continue to falter. It is also a calculated measure to potentially help Butker rediscover his typical accuracy. Tucker regressed during his final season with the Baltimore Ravens and missed a career-high eight of his 30 attempts, and Toub detailed how it could be beneficial for Butker to receive mentorship from one of the league's greatest kickers of all time -- one who recently dealt with accuracy struggles of his own.Tucker missed the entire 2025 season while he served a 10-game suspension following an investigation into alleged inappropriate behaviors during massage sessions. He became eligible to sign with a new team ahead of the 2026 season and received numerous calls before the Chiefs landed him.
"He's a good kicker," Toub said. "I've heard he's been out making the rounds. We talk. All the special teams coaches talk. He had four workouts before we brought him in. We were his fifth workout, tryout. The word was that he's hitting the ball great. I wanted to see it. I always thought he was a great kicker."Toub constructed a 30-kick tryout for Tucker and the other candidates that included 10 extra points, seven field goals of over 50 yards and one 60-yarder. Tucker went 30-for-30, and 60% of his conversions landed inside a six-foot cylinder in the middle of the uprights."Somebody that's struggling is not able to put the ball with that kind of accuracy at 30 kicks," Toub said. "He was off-the-charts good. That's the reason why we signed him to the practice squad."
With Tucker seemingly back in the kind of form that made him a Ravens legend, he could be a viable option on game days if called upon.

        Last week many of us expected Lamar Jackson to return to face the Cincinnati Bengals. That turned out to be premature. In Week 8, we are feeling more confident in Jackson's return, partially because he practiced in full on Wednesday. Jackson and the Ravens will face the Buffalo Bills in Week 8, which is a fantastic matchup. The Bills have given up 29 or more points in every game but one this season, and Jackson is a top-six QB in his return even though we have some concern about whether he will run as much as he typically does. His return puts Zay Flowers inside the top five at receiver and boosts Derrick Henry back inside the top 12 despite some uninspiring efficiency this season.Here's what else we're monitoring on Thursday:Emeka Egbuka working his way backEgbuka is still in the concussion protocol and has a foot injury, but there is reason to be optimistic about his return. He was at practice on Wednesday in a non-contact jersey and showed up on Thursday in his regular jersey. We aren't 100% sure he'll play, but we are confident enough to rank him as a number three receiver. You should still start Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker, Christian Watson, and Matthew Golden (if he's active) over Egbuka on Thursday night. His return makes Chris Godwin far less appealing as a number three receiver.The Eagles' injury situation not getting better yetSaquon Barkley, Devonta Smith, and Dontayvion Wicks all missed practice on Wednesday, and none of them were seen at the early portion of Thursday's practice. The team also placed Dameon Pierce on Injured Reserve earlier in this week. The top two healthy running backs at this time are Jaydon Blue and Elijah Mitchell, who is still on the practice squad. We would expect an elevation for Mitchell if Barkley can't go and would view him as the best Eagles running back, though we wouldn't want to start Mitchell or Blue. If Smith and Wicks remain out, then Makai Lemon is a good WR3 in full PPR leagues. Dallas Goedert looks like a must-start tight end as well.DJ Moore in non-contact jersey for second day in a rowThis is a big one, and we don't have much clarity on it yet. Moore is dealing with a shoulder injury, and it is a positive that he is practicing, but the uncertainty remains because he has not yet been cleared for contact. If he plays, we will view him as a WR2 with upside in a shootout against the Ravens. If Moore is out, then Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir are attractive WR3 options, though Coleman would be our favorite.
Rashee Rice working his way back from hamstring injuryRice practiced for a second straight day and could be on track for a Week 8 return. Unfortunately, he's facing the Denver Broncos, who are also expected to get Patrick Surtain back. Rice's return would be a big hit to Xavier Worthy, who is a WR3 without Rice and a low-end flex with Rice. Travis Kelce would also take a bit of a hit, but he would probably remain a top 12 tight end. If Rice is able to return, view him as a WR3 in a very tough matchup.A.J. Brown trending the wrong wayBrown missed practice on Thursday after a limited session on Wednesday, putting his Week 8 status in doubt. We have him ranked as a low-end WR2 because of his upside, but it is getting harder to believe he is healthy enough to show it. Drake Maye would still be a top 12 QB without Brown, but not one we would be very excited about. Demario Douglas would be the best Patriots wide receiver without Brown. Hunter Henry and Maye are the only sure starters on this team, and Rhamondre Stevenson is a low-end RB2 in a great matchup. TreVeyon Henderson also missed practice on Thursday, which could make Stevenson a better play.Tyjae Spears and Carnell Tate both miss practice on ThursdayThis is two days in a row, and you should at least have a backup plan if you are planning on starting Tate, who is a solid WR2 in our rankings. Spears didn't play last week, and it's increasingly likely we will get another week of Tony Pollard as a workhorse. The Bengals recently shut down Derrick Henry, so this may be a bad matchup, but Pollard is a solid RB2 if Spears is out, given his increased work in the passing game. Tony Pollard was also not seen at practice on Thursday, but we don't think his status is in question.Ladd McConkey working way through concussion protocolIt is looking more like McConkey could return in Week 8, though it is no sure thing on Thursday afternoon. This is not a very good matchup against the Rams, and the Chargers have been a disaster offensively, so we wouldn't view McConkey as more than a WR3. We would prefer to sit all Chargers against the Rams this week.
Jadarian Price has his practice window openedGood grief. The Seahawks may have both Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price back in Week 8. Honestly, no one has any reason to have any confidence in who would lead this backfield in touches. The only thing we feel confident in is that Emanuel Wilson is no longer a good RB2 for Fantasy purposes. No Seahawks back should be viewed as more than a flex in Week 8.

title: Jason Kelce rants, calls out refs over unnecessary roughness penalty on Giants' Cam Skattebo - CBS Sports
description: The Kelce brothers did not mince words when they voiced displeasure with the NFL's officials
body:
The Kelce brothers did not mince words when they voiced displeasure with the NFL's officials

    3:54 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo might be the most physical ballcarrier in the NFL, and sometimes that gets him in trouble. Officials in the Week 7 game against the Houston Texans called Skattebo for a controversial penalty on a first-quarter run when they deemed him guilty of a rarely enforced unnecessary roughness infraction. The penalty flag thrown on the play drew immense scrutiny, and Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce on the "New Heights" podcast joined the chorus of prominent football figures to stand up for Skattebo.The officials penalized Skattebo for lowering his helmet against a Texans defender. It was just the fourth time this season that foul has been called and the first time it went against an offensive player on a non-special teams play.
Travis Kelce, a physical player in his own right, scoffed at the penalty and said, "That's football." Jason Kelce took an even more passionate stance against the call."If the running back hits the defensive player with the crown of his helmet, and you get run over, that's the defensive guy's fault," Jason Kelce said. "Hit him in the f---ing legs. What are we talking about? You're the one who tried to tackle him up top. What the f---? I think it's a dumbass penalty. I think that the runner should have the ability to lower his shoulder and gain yardage however he wants. And if his head goes down with it, that's the way it should be.
"I'm not a fan of the way this is called. I understand it's a penalty, and this is how they want it officiated. I actually think he more just lowered his shoulders. I didn't think he actually lowered his head as much as I've seen."
The 15-yard penalty did not prove costly for the Giants, as they proceeded to defeat the Texans in overtime. But it did set a precedent that could impact Skattebo's future games. He said he will not change his running style and that if he continues to draw penalties or faces league-imposed fines, then so be it."It was more of he just ran the f---ing dude over," Jason Kelce said, "and the guy was embarrassed, and he lied there for a second, and the league was like, 'Oh, we gotta fine Cam Skattebo.' That's the f---ing dumbest G--damn thing I've ever seen. It's f---ing stupid."
While Skattebo found himself in the doghouse with coach John Harbaugh the previous week due to his early-season fumbling issues, his coach has his back in this case. Harbaugh said it would be a "physical impossibility" for a running back like Skattebo to avoid lowering his head when carrying the ball low to the ground and praised his second-year standout for good fundamentals.Travis Kelce sees it the same way."How do you -- you go flat? Eyes, head up? What's the position? You have to get into a specific position? If he's just trying to lower his pads and accelerate?"The penalty was a minor hiccup for Skattebo in what was otherwise the best performance of his career. He racked up a personal-best 124 yards and a touchdown against the Texans and set up the game-winning play in overtime when he broke loose for a 42-yard scamper.

A 13-6 win in overtime against a listless Michigan team didn't assuage those concerns, and now they welcome a Minnesota team that has proven to be a thorny opponent. The Gophers come in at 5-2 fresh off a 13-10 win over Iowa to hoist the Floyd of Rosedale trophy, as PJ Fleck is 2-for-2 in rivalry games this season. Minnesota will need to step up their level in the next two games against top-10 foes in Indiana and UCLA, but if the Hoosiers get caught looking ahead to a trip to USC, they can quickly find themselves in a dogfight with the Gophers despite being 20.5-point favorites. Will the Hoosiers' offense come to life back at home and re-establish themselves as one of the nation's elite? Can Minnesota pull off another stunner by dragging Indiana into the mud? We'll find out on Saturday afternoon in what could be another thrilling, tense Big Ten battle. 
  Minnesota vs. Indiana: Need to know  Hoosiers need more from Hoover: Indiana's still a top 5 team, but this is clearly not a squad at the same level as last year. That's largely due to an offense stuck in the mud, with a quarterback who has not clicked with the scheme despite two highly talented receivers on the outside. Josh Hoover has been dreadful the last few weeks, and when the Hoosiers have won, it's been in spite of their quarterback's play. That might not need to change to win this week specifically, but the Hoosiers are desperate to establish some form of offensive rhythm in the back half of the season before the College Football Playoff. The Gophers present challenges, but this is the caliber of team Indiana should be able to handle with ease. They've not proven to have that gear so far this season, and it's incumbent on Hoover to be both more dynamic and more efficient throwing the football for them to find that next level. 
DE-FENSE [clapclapclap]: The defenses for both teams are their point of strength, and both teams will be looking to their defensive playmakers to help them out. The Hoosiers and Gophers put forward defensive masterclasses in low-scoring wins a week ago, but Minnesota is the team with the greater questions on that side of the ball. There have been games where Minnesota looks fantastic defensively (like last week against Iowa), but they have struggled against teams that can stretch the field and have high-level athletes on the outside. Indiana has that in Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh, but the question is whether Josh Hoover can get them the ball on time and on target regularly enough to take advantage of their mismatches. Indiana has no such questions, and they'll start by trying to take away Minnesota's ground game and dare Drake Lindsey to beat them through the air. 
Can Drake Lindsey protect the football? There's a world where the Gophers hang around in this one and are a live dog on the road to pull a stunning upset. However, that only happens if Lindsey protects the football, something he's not excelled at this season. Lindsey leads the Big Ten with six interceptions and has thrown at least one in each of Minnesota's last five games. The Gophers have to maximize every possession to have a chance against Indiana, and given the Hoosiers have an elite defense, there won't be any room for error on Lindsey's part. He came into the season with NFL Draft buzz because of his physical tools, but he's got to manage risk better in the second half of the season to boost that stock. TV: CBS | Live stream: CBSSports.com, CBS Sports App  Streaming on Paramount+ Premium  Minnesota vs. Indiana prediction, picks  If it ain't broke, don't fix it. The lack of trust in Hoover is never more apparent than when he trots the punt unit out on a fourth-and-short at midfield without hesitation. Even if Indiana dominates, it's hard to see them piling up points on a good Minnesota defense, and there's a real world where the Gophers keep this close throughout. How to bet on horse racing: Most popular types of wagers There are a plethora of different wagering options available on each race. We will go through the three traditional bets – Win, Place and Show – as well as the combinations of each. Below are horse racing betting tips that identify bet types and the differences between the odds found at sportsbook and racing odds.  Each horse will have different odds for each bet type. These odds let you know the horse's expected return on each individual bet type. It's important to note that the odds on each horse fluctuate constantly and payouts are calculated based on the final odds, not the exact odds from the time you place your bet, a major difference from betting on other sports.               Differences in horse racing odds vs. sportsbook odds             Horse racing odds rely on pari-mutuel wagering, which is a system that pools together all of the money bet on each market up until the race begins. The track and the books take a certain percentage or rake for their operations (the Takeout), and the remainder of the pool is then divided among the winning ticket holders. The takeout is divided between the house (track) and horsemen, including race purses.               What is particularly unique about this system for those who are accustomed to betting on sports is that your odds can shift after you place the bet until they lock when the race begins. On sports betting apps, if you bet something at 10-1 and it later moves to 8-1, you still receive the 10-1 payout. In horse racing, your payout will change based on the way the market moves to create the final odds. The final odds you'll receive are determined by how much is bet on each horse and the Takeout.              The standard horse racing unit for win, place, or show bets is $2.                         Win             The win bet is simply betting on which horse will come in first place. Using the 2026 Herbie Dyke Stakes as an example, the winner was Legarto and finished with 12-5 odds. A $2 Win bet paid $6.80, a product of the standard $4.80 for a 12-5 payout on a $2 bet, plus your original $2 wager amount back.                          Place             The Place bet allows you to wager on whether a horse will finish first or second in a race, meaning two Place bets will pay out on each race. This gives you a greater chance of winning, but lowers your odds on the horse if they place.              Using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as the example again, a $2 Place bet on the No. 18 horse only returned $7.50 compared to the $17.96 for a Win bet. But also, a $2 Place bet on the No. 8 horse (Journalism), who was the favorite but came in second, paid $4.94 while the Win bet lost.                           Show             A Show bet is a highly conservative betting option. You are wagering on whether a horse will finish in the top three positions. That means three Show bets will pay out each race. For example, a $2 Show bet on a 10-1 winner returned $4. As one might expect, show bet odds are far less favorable than win bet odds, making them one of the more conservative wagers available in horse racing.                           Win/Place             Additionally, you can combine these bets on each horse when you're placing your wagers. That means if you want to bet on a horse to win and place, you can do that. A $2 Win/Place bet really means you're betting $4 – a $2 Win bet and a $2 Place bet. If the horse you bet on wins, you will win both bets. If the horse finishes second, you would only win the Place bet.                           Place/Show             The same is available for a Place/Show bet, where a $2 Place/Show bet would be $4 wagered on a $2 Place bet and a $2 Show bet. If your horse finishes first or second, you would win both, but if it finishes third, you would only win the Show bet.                           Win/Place/Show (Across The Board)              Lastly, you can bet on all three options in what is often referred to as an Across The Board bet. A $2 Across The Board bet would really be $6 wagered – $2 on Win, $2 on Place, and $2 on Show. If you make an Across The Board bet and your horse wins, you pay out on all three wagers.              It's important to note that betting on Win/Place/Show combinations may not result in a net return even if one of the bets pays. For example, at the 2024 Kentucky Derby, an Across The Board bet on the 11 horse would've returned just $5.58 on $6 wagered.                           The most popular horse racing bet types             Many horse racing bettors place exotic bets to try to predict where multiple horses will finish in a race. These combination wagers offer the chance for bigger payouts, but come with a lower probability of winning (just like same game parlays in sports betting).              It is important to note that, unlike sports betting, there is no standard odds calculation to use for determining exotic payouts. Because of parimutuel wagering, odds can fluctuate until the race begins based on which horses are taking the most action. Additionally, live horse racing betting is available, adding another layer of entertainment for those watching races as they take place.               Exactas             An exacta bet in horse racing functions the same as it does across other sports. The bettor must pick the exact finishing order. For example, if someone wants to place an exacta bet with two horses, they must select each horse and where it will finish exactly. Once again using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as an example, a $2 exacta on the No. 18 and No. 8 horses (who closed with final odds of 7-1 and almost 3-1) paid $48.32. This style of betting can be seen in plenty of other sports, especially in futures betting.  Exotics winnings will vary based on the number of horses in the race, the odds of the top-finishing horses, and the size of the pool. For example, the field for the 2024 Kentucky Derby saw a longer shot horse win, so the exacta pool paid $258.56 -- significantly more than the 2025 Derby.                           Trifectas             This horse racing wager is placing a bet on the exact order of the top-three finishers in a race. A straight trifecta will pay handsomely, but is extremely difficult to hit. Trifecta payouts are often shown for $0.50 bets, but some will show for $1 bets as well. The payout screen will tell you which, but that's important to note so you're aware of how much you are getting back.              The 2025 Kentucky Derby Trifecta paid $231.12 on a $1 Trifecta bet.                           Superfectas             Superfecta bets try to predict the exact order of the top-four finishers in a horse race. The superfecta payout is usually shown for a $1 bet. For the 2025 Kentucky Derby, a $1 superfecta that added the fourth-place No. 3 horse to the trifecta paid $1,682.27.                          Super High 5             Some books will allow you to bet on the top-five finishers in their exact order in what is called a Super High 5 bet. Those payouts will again be shown for a $1 wager. The odds of hitting a Super High 5, especially in a large field race, are exceptionally low. They are equivalent to multi-leg futures parlays in sports betting.  The 2025 Kentucky Derby's $1 Super High Five paid $38,405.96.                          Box             A box bet allows you to have every possible combination for exotics. If you think you know which two horses will hit the exacta but are not sure of their specific order, you can box it. The same goes for trifectas and superfectas. The more horses you box together, the lower your total profits on the payout will be.              For example, a three-horse exacta box bet costs $12 to bet, as you are betting $2 on all six potential combinations between those three horses:             $2 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 3 second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 1 in first and No. 3 in secondYou can do the same for Trifectas and Superfectas, but at exponentially escalating costs. A $1 Trifecta Box with three horses is six combinations, so $6 wagered:             $1 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 1 in first, No. 3 in second, No. 2 in first$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 2 in third$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 1 in firstFrom there, four horses in a $1 trifecta box is 24 combinations for $24 wagered. Five horses make 60 possible combinations for $60.              A $1 Superfecta box of four horses is $24 wagered, five horses is $120 wagered and six horses is $360 wagered.                           How to bet on horse racing: Multi-race wagers             While those exotics offer a variety of options for betting on individual races, you can also bet on multiple races at the same track in various ways. These combination wagers pay out based on the betting pool, allowing you to choose a handful of horses you're confident in throughout the day to increase your potential payout.                           Daily Double             The Daily Double is exactly what it sounds like: Betting on back-to-back race winners from that day. The odds for Daily Doubles vary based on the odds for the individual horses you bet and the overall Daily Double betting pool. As an example, the $2 Daily Double at Horseshoe Indianapolis on April 15, 2025 from the first two races with the 7 horse in the first race (went off at 1-1 odds) and the 4 horse in the second race (went off at 3-5 odds) paid $8.              Once the first race ends, the payouts for each potential Daily Double will be shown under a "Will Pays" tab on the next race's betting screen.                           Pick-3, Pick-4, Pick-5 and Pick-6             Along with the Daily Double, there are more options for betting the winner of multiple races in a row at the same track. The Pick-3 is picking the winner in three consecutive races, the Pick-4 in four consecutive races, and so on for the Pick-5 and Pick-6.             Like exotics, the pool amount and the odds for each horse wagered on determine the payouts for these multi-race wagers. The default unit for these bets varies from book to book, with FanDuel showing $0.50 payouts and TwinSpires showing $1 payouts in the Will Pays section.              The more races you put together on a ticket, the more you can win. But as with any multi-race wager, the more legs you add, the harder it is to win. In this way, these bets function similarly to parlays in other sports.  For some of the biggest races, the Pick-6 will feature a set guaranteed prize pool for the winner(s) no matter what the actual wagered amount is. The 2024 Kentucky Derby featured a $1 million guaranteed pool on TwinSpires for Pick-6s on races 6 through 11 at Churchill Downs.                           Understanding horse racing payouts             After the race, the winning payouts will be displayed for each bet type. The standard unit for win/place/show and exactas is a $2 bet. Trifectas, superfectas and super high 5s are typically shown as $1 or $0.50, but will say explicitly which on the payout board.              The payouts for each horse in the top three for the 2025 Kentucky Derby looked as follows:             2025 Kentucky DerbyWinPlaceShowSovereignty (No. 18) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$17.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$7.50 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$5.58 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Journalism (No. 8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								             $4.94 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$3.70 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Baeza (No. 21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								             				             $8.38 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				             If you bet more (or less) than the standard $2 unit, you multiply the payout by how much you bet and divide by the standard unit. For example, a $10 Win bet on Sovereignty returned $89.80, while a $25 Show bet on Journalism would've returned $46.25.              For the single-race exotics at the 2025 Kentucky Derby, the payouts were as follows:              2025 Kentucky DerbyPayout$2 Exacta (18-8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$48.32 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Trifecta (18-8-21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$231.12 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Superfecta (18-8-21-3) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1,682.27 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Super High 5 (18-8-21-3-20) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$38,405.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				            Biggest horse races beyond Kentucky Derby betting            The horse racing calendar operates year-round, but there are six events on the schedule that serve as the most important, thus attracting the best fields. The three Triple Crown events headline for the general public, but the Breeders' Cup, Pegasus World Cup and Dubai World Cup all offer massive purses and attract some of the best horses and fields in all of racing.             October 30-31, 2026: Breeders' Cup January 23, 2027: Pegasus World CupMarch 27, 2027: Dubai World CupMay 1, 2027: Kentucky DerbyMay 15, 2027: Preakness StakesJune 5, 2027: Belmont Stakes             Triple Crown of horse racing             The Kentucky Derby, Preakness Stakes and Belmont Stakes make up horse racing's Triple Crown. There are 13 horses that have completed the Triple Crown, winning all three events, and only two – American Pharoah (2015) and Justify (2018) – have accomplished that feat in the 21st century.              Not every horse competes in all three Triple Crown events. Each race operates at different lengths, and the turnaround time can be too quick for trainers to be comfortable running their horse in one after the other. Some Derby winners don't run the Preakness, while some have made it two legs before withdrawing from the Belmont.              The Kentucky Derby is a 1 1/4 mile race, the Preakness Stakes is 1 3/16 mile, and the Belmont Stakes is a grueling 1 1/2 mile event (although it is being run currently at 1 1/4 mile at Saratoga Race Course due to renovations at Belmont Park).                           Tips and advice for betting on horse racing             There are a number of strategies for betting on horse racing, but it all starts with understanding the horses and knowing their strengths, weaknesses and past performances.                           Racing forms and past performances             Racing forms are race-day publications and programs available at tracks and online to preview the day's races at each track. They are full of data and information from past races. All of the best horse racing betting apps have integrated much of this information into their betting screen.                           Track conditions             Before you even get to the horses, understanding track conditions is vital. Knowing if a track is dirt or grass, firm and fast or soft and slow, is critical information to know so you can look at which horses in a given race run best in certain conditions.                           Horse tendencies              From there, you want to understand the tendencies of horses in the field. Some horses get out to fast starts and try to push the pace, while others hang back and try to make a late kick. If most of the field is expected to push the pace and run it fast, then a horse that prefers to stay back may be at an advantage due to its advantage in a late-game run.              The opposite could be true, too; if the pace is going to be slower early, frontrunners are more likely to hold their position. Some of this information can be found in PPs or Past Performance data.                           Post position             Post position can also matter to a horse's success. Some prefer to run the rail (on the inside of the track) while others prefer being on the outside and running with more space around them. This information is all worth considering and comparing with the other horses in the field.                          Trainer and jockey information             A horse's trainer and jockey will also have tendencies. Some trainers are better at getting horses ready for a certain type of track, but maybe don't have a great track record at others. Some jockeys may be more or less aggressive on the track, which may or may not work well with that specific horse's tendencies, or they may have a long track record with that horse and know how to get the most out of them.                           Workout times             There's also plenty of data available that can help you. Workout times, if available, can give you an idea of how a horse has been running in training before a big race.                           Speed figures             Speed figures are like advanced stats of the horse racing world, offering a metric to show how well a horse has been running in its recent races that factors in things like field strength and track quality.              Taking all of that data into account is important to betting on horse racing, and for beginners it's best to ease in and do as much observing as you do betting. You'll start to find certain trends for horses, jockeys, trainers and tracks that can help you find edges on the odds board going forward.                          Manage your horse racing betting bankroll             Managing your bankroll with what percentage of money you have set aside for horse racing betting is vital to increasing your chances of scoring big at some point. Just like in sports betting, where most bankroll management experts advise no more than 2% of your bankroll should be bet on any given game, the same principle can be applied to any given horse race.                           Rules and responsible gaming             Responsible gambling is taken very seriously across all racebooks. All provide the necessary resources and contact information if you or someone you know may have a gambling problem. The minimum age is 18 for horse racing betting in most states, but it is 21 in some states.             Responsible gambling resources include the National Council for Problem Gambling (NCPG) and Gamblers Anonymous. Be smart. Bet smart. Wager responsibly. Those in need of help can also call or text 1-800-GAMBLER (1-800-426-2537). Help is available 24 hours a day and seven days a week.               FAQ    How to bet on horse racing?  There are several ways to bet on horse racing. The most common methods are through horse racing betting apps like TwinSpires, FanDuel Racing, and DraftKings Horse. Users can bet on a variety of outcomes, with the most common wager coming on which horse will win the given race outright.    How to bet on horse racing online?  Online horse racing betting is widely accessible. TwinSpires, DraftKings Horse, and FanDuel Racing all provide users with a huge array of betting options on all major races.    What is a box bet in horse racing?  A box bet in horse racing involves picking the finishing order of the horses. Wagerers can choose the order of the first two, three, four, or five finishers, with the return on their bet increasing with every additional horse they include in their wager. If a bettor chooses three horses for a box bet, they do not need to finish in an exact order. If they make up the top three, the bet is successful.    What is a show bet in horse racing?  A show bet is a wager on a specific horse to finish among the top three horses in a given race. Show bets are extremely common wagers that offer less risk and smaller payouts.    What is a key box bet in horse racing?  A key box bet, unsurprisingly, functions similarly to a box bet. A bettor can select a "key" horse that they believe will finish in an exact position while rounding out the rest of the box in the same fashion as a regular box bet. For example, a bettor could select Horse A to finish first while picking Horses C, B, and D to round out the top four. However, if Horse A does not finish first, the bet loses.

Their last meeting came in the 2017 Cotton Bowl. Prior to that, they hadn't played since the 2009 season. It took until USC's third season as a Big Ten member for the two to appear on each other's schedules, but this Saturday night the wait will end.And it's a game that got a lot more intriguing in recent weeks. USC enters the game unranked for the first time all season following a 17-7 loss at Wisconsin last week. While Ohio State remains second in the AP Top 25, this will be the team's first game since losing starting quarterback Julian Sayin, who was knocked out of their 19-15 win over Indiana.Ohio State vs. USC: Need to know  This will be Luke Fahey's first career start: On the surface, giving your quarterback his first career start on the road is not an ideal situation, but it's one Ohio State has had success with before. In 2001, Craig Krenzel started his first game on the road against Michigan of all teams, and Ohio State won that game 26-20. In 2013, it was Kenny Guiton winning his first start at Cal, and in 2021, CJ Stroud won his first start at Minnesota.  There's a lot on the line for Jeremiah Smith: Smith is the best receiver in the country and is already Ohio State's all-time leader in career receptions, yards, and touchdowns, just to name a few stats. He's also the clear favorite to win the Heisman Trophy, but this will be his first start with Fahey as well. It's safe to assume Smith will be Fahey's preferred target, but it remains to be seen whether he can maintain the same level of production and how that may impact his Heisman chances.

title: Could Big Ten turn to NFL-style scheduling model? Ohio State AD hints at change - CBS Sports
description: According to Bjork, the Big Ten is exploring a dynamic new model that could go into effect in 2028
body:
According to Bjork, the Big Ten is exploring a dynamic new model that could go into effect in 2028
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 29, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:06 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Big Ten has already adopted what amounts to a salary cap in college athletics, and now it might take another step toward mimicking the NFL with its approach to scheduling. Ohio State athletic director Ross Bjork said the conference is looking at a results-based scheduling model.Bjork joined "The Ryan Day Show" on 97.1 The Fan and shared some insight about discussions around scheduling. Bjork noted that -- when the Big Ten first expanded to include the West Coast teams -- scheduling rotations were based upon historical records in football.Well, teams like Indiana are in a very different place now than they were even five years ago."They looked at historical rotations over the course of everyone's football life," Bjork said. "Indiana was not what Indiana is today when they set the model. Same thing with UCLA."
Bjork said changes could begin with the 2028 season, explaining that opponents wouldn't be set in stone until after the 2027 campaign. The Big Ten would use a dynamic scheduling model, like the NFL's, based on the previous season's results. Worse teams would get more favorable slates. Better teams would get tougher matchups.The one major difference is that the Big Ten would ensure key rivalries, like Ohio State vs. Michigan, remain in place every year."So, next year's schedule, we would not know who we're playing, other than protecting the rivalry games," Bjork said. "Obviously, we have the biggest one. Other than that, the rest of the schedule could be based on how the teams finished the previous year. That's how the NFL does it."
Bjork said a new model is required due to the parity created by NIL and the transfer portal. A dynamic scheduling model could be a more equitable way to balance strength of schedule across the league."We're having active conversations that we need to change the way we schedule," Bjork said. "... There's a lot more parity in the system."One potential flaw in adopting the NFL's model is that current transfer portal and NIL rules allow limitless player movement every offseason. That creates much more volatility from one season to the next, unlike in the NFL, where multi-year contracts create more roster stability.
It's an intriguing idea, though, and scheduling will be a hot topic with the 24-team College Football Playoff arriving soon.

The son of former NBA player Rafer "Skip 2 My Lou" Alston, Reese is the third member of LSU's 2027 recruiting class, and the first five-star Wade has landed since returning

        Five-star guard Reese Alston, the son of former NBA guard Rafer "Skip 2 My Lou" Alston, committed to LSU on CBS Sports HQ on Thursday. Alston, who is the No. 9 overall player in the 2027 recruiting cycle by 247Sports, picked the Tigers over Louisville, Kentucky, Tennessee and Wichita State.The Houston Second Baptist product is now the third member of LSU's 2027 recruiting class, joining four-star combo guard King Gibson and Ahmad Hudson, who is also committed to the Tigers football team as a five-star tight end. With the addition of Alston, the Tigers have the No.2-ranked recruiting class for the 2027 cycle. He is also the first five-star high school recruit Will Wade has landed since returning to LSU.With three high school players already committed this cycle, it signals a new approach for Wade to build his roster for the 2027-28 season, after relying heavily on the transfer portal and international players to build it out heading into the 2026-27 season. Wade has been outspoken about his "unconventional roster," which features several players fighting in court for a fifth year of eligibility.
247Sports Director of Scouting says that Alston can consistently "create offense for himself and his teammates."He's an offensive engine who both thrives and is most comfortable as the primary domino in his team's attack. He has adequate positional size and length, deceptive strength and balance through contact, good open floor speed, and some sneaky leaping ability when he has a runway. He's also an underrated on-ball defender who is capable of picking up for the length of the floor, even though that's not what he's known for at this point.Alston is just the latest top-20-ranked player in his recruiting class to announce his commitment. This week, four-star forward Asa Montgomery committed to Duke, while five-star center Lewis Uvwo committed to Providence on Wednesday and became the highest-ranked player in the upcoming recruiting cycle to make a commitment.
In CBS Sports' report that broke down the NIL arms race in college basketball, LSU ranked in Tier 3, which is a budget range of $15.1 million to $17.5 million. In that tier, LSU was notably joined by Miami, Arizona, USC, Michigan State and SEC foes Missouri, Auburn, Oklahoma, Vanderbilt and South Carolina.
